question: Proposed restrictions on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) could have a significant impact on access to medicines and medical devices that are crucial for our healthcare. These substances are currently used broadly in the manufacturing of medical devices and medicines, in application devices such as syringes or pens, and in packaging for sterility and effectiveness.

Currently, the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) is evaluating a proposal by Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, Sweden and Norway to restrict PFAS, including for medical devices and medicines. Limiting exposure to PFAS is of key importance for our environment and public health.

However, given the essential role of PFAS for medicines and medical devices, I am concerned about how a PFAS ban in this area could disrupt supply and affect the delivery of healthcare. In the light of the above, I ask the Commission: 1.
To avoid disruptions to healthcare, what steps will the Commission take to prevent the supply of these products being negatively affected by any potential ban?

In exchanges with the five Member States concerned and the ECHA, will the Commission support prioritising the evaluation of PFAS in medical devices and medicines, as well as giving timely disclosure of any exemptions, as specific measures to prevent disruption?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.7.2024) In line with provisions set out in Title VIII of Regulation (EU) 1907/2006 (REACH)1, the Commission is awaiting the results of the scientific assessment of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) restrictions by the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA).

The Commission has not been involved in the preparation of the REACH restriction dossier on PFAS submitted by five European countries2. However, the Commission is closely following the opinion development by ECHA and will be an observer during the Risk Assessment Committee (RAC) and Socio-Economic Analysis Committee (SEAC) meetings.

The restriction dossier already contains a proposal for some derogations for the use of PFAS in medical devices and medicinal products. The need for derogations will be carefully assessed by RAC and SEAC. An analysis of alternatives and of the socio-economic impact is part of the assessment.

As soon as the RAC and SEAC opinions are finalised, the Commission will consider possible restrictions of PFAS taking into account risks of disruptions in the medical device and the medicinal product sectors.
1 Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 December 2006

concerning the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH), establishing a European Chemicals Agency, amending Directive 1999/45/EC and repealing Council Regulation (EEC) No 793/93 and Commission Regulation (EC) No 1488/94 as well as Council Directive 76/769/EEC and Commission Directives 91/155/EEC, 93/67/EEC, 93/105/EC and 2000/21/EC http://data.europa.
